transcript.text: My Beko keeps stopping randomly in the middle of a wash with water still in it. Sometimes it's fine for a week, then it does it twice in a day. The model starts WTG I think. I've cleaned the filter. Driving me mad.

Since cleaning the filter hasn't fixed it, we need to see how the machine handles the draining phase, as that is what must happen before it can spin. Please run a 'Spin' or 'Drain' programme only. While it is trying to pump the water out, listen closely near the bottom front of the machine. Also, does the water actually leave the drum?

I haven't tried a drain-only programme, so I can't say if the water goes out on that one. When it stalls mid-wash I've noticed the pump sometimes runs for a second or two and then just stops. Is that any help?

Yes, that detail helps significantly. A pump running briefly and then stopping usually means it has hit an obstruction (like a coin, button, or hair ball) or a jammed impeller, causing the machine to cut power to protect itself before it can empty the water. With the machine switched off and unplugged, remove the filter cover again. Shine a torch into the hole and gently try to turn the small plastic fan (impeller) with your finger or a non-metallic tool. Does it spin freely, is it stuck/jammed by something, or are the vanes broken?

Well, I cleaned the filter twice and only found fluff in it, nothing like a coin or button. I haven't looked at the impeller though, I'm not sure I'd know what I was looking at. Is it likely to be that if the filter was clean?

Yes, it is very likely to be that even with a clean filter. The filter catches large items like coins, but smaller objects (like a sock fragment, hair ball, or small button) can get trapped in the pump impeller just behind it, or further down in the sump hose. Since checking the filter didn't fix it, let's check if the water is actually flowing out of the machine at all. With the machine switched off and unplugged, pull the drain hose (usually at the back) away from the wall slightly. Place the end in a bucket on the floor and tilt it down to see if any water trickles out freely. Does it drain quickly, or is there no water/movement?

Ok, I could try that, though the hose goes into a standpipe and it's a bit awkward to pull out. The hose itself is fine, no kinks, and the water does go away normally on the washes that finish. Do I really need to do the bucket thing, or is there something simpler?

No, you don't need to do the bucket test if you know the water drains normally when a cycle finishes—that just suggests the external plumbing and hose aren't completely blocked. The fact that it stops mid-wash with water inside, combined with the pump running briefly then stopping, strongly suggests something is partially blocking the pump impeller (the small plastic fan behind the filter). It hits an obstruction, strains, and the machine cuts power to protect itself. Since you haven't checked the impeller yet, please remove the filter again. With the machine switched off and unplugged, shine a torch into the hole and gently try to turn the small plastic fan (impeller) with your finger. Does it spin freely, is it stuck/jammed by something, or are the vanes broken?

Hmm, I'm honestly not sure how to check that properly, I wouldn't know what I was looking at in there with a torch. I'm not taking any panels off either. Is there anything else it could be that I can check from the outside?

Since you aren't comfortable checking inside the filter housing or removing panels, we have reached the limit of what is safe and practical for you to do at home. Because these components are located inside the machine casing, they require dismantling to access and clear or replace. I would recommend calling a qualified engineer to inspect the pump assembly; it is likely that clearing a hidden blockage or replacing the pump will resolve the issue.
